name: Lovage
grown_as: A long-lived perennial herb grown for its strong celery-flavoured leaves
habit: A big leafy clump 1.5 to 2 m tall in flower and about 1 m across, from a stout crown. Stems thick, hollow, smooth, hairless, branching above. Strong smell of celery.

leaf.arrangement: Large leaves from the base; alternate and smaller up the stems
leaf.type: Compound, two or three times pinnate, with broad leaflets
leaf.leaflets: Broadly wedge- to diamond-shaped, 3 to 10 cm, often three-lobed
leaf.outline: The whole leaf triangular to diamond-shaped, up to 60 cm or more
leaf.base: Leaflets narrowing to an untoothed wedge base
leaf.margin: A few coarse irregular teeth and shallow lobes on the upper half of each leaflet only; the lower wedge smooth
leaf.veins: Pinnate, visible but not deeply pressed in
leaf.surface: Smooth, hairless and glossy, like celery
leaf.stalk: Long, stout, green, with a broad sheathing base
leaf.colour: Dark glossy green; young spring shoots reddish-bronze

flower.petals: Five tiny petals per flower, incurved
flower.centre: Tiny yellowish stamens and a swollen base
flower.behind: Several narrow bracts under the umbel and bracteoles under each small umbel, turned down, with pale papery edges
flower.carried: At the top of tall stems and branches, facing up, on 12 to 20 rays

fruit: Oblong flattened seeds 5 to 7 mm in pairs, yellowish-brown, with ribs edged by narrow wings
seedling: Two long narrow seed leaves, then first true leaves three-lobed and toothed
winter: Dies right down to the crown. Reddish-bronze shoots push up in early spring. Dead hollow stems may stand.

leaf: large leaf divided two or three times into broad leaflets
leaflets wedge-based with coarse teeth on the upper half only
bloom: bracts and bracteoles turned down under the umbels
seed: oblong flat seed with winged ribs, yellowish-brown
young: glossy celery-like leaves on long stalks from the crown
crop: a big dense clump of glossy dark green divided leaves
flower: tall stout stems to about 2 m
large divided leaves at the base
dormant: nothing above ground or dead stems only
reddish shoots at the crown in late winter

look_alikes: Celery has fleshy grooved stalks, smaller greenish-white umbels without bracts and is shorter. Garden angelica (Angelica archangelica) has rounder green umbels and leaflets toothed all round. Alexanders (Smyrnium olusatrum) has leaves in threes and black seeds.
